categories.reason: Owner mode, also without a label scheme, keeps persistence off. SAVE, BGSAVE, BGREWRITEAOF, DUMP, RESTORE, MIGRATE, DEBUG RELOAD and DEBUG LOADAOF answer the persistence error, also before a transaction's own refusal of SAVE, and CONFIG SET of save points or of appendonly yes is refused, so tests that save, reload, dump, restore or switch the append-only file on differ. A test that reads a dump an earlier, refused test should have made fails as well, and a start_server block with appendonly yes ends the rest of type/stream and type/stream-cgroups.

categories.reason: Without a label scheme every login runs at the one label, which is top, but a login without an owner rule acts as SHARED, and without the owner-operator rule it has no operator scope. Such a login sees none of the data the suite's login writes as suite-user, INFO shows it no statistics, top-only commands such as CONFIG RESETSTAT are refused with the owner-operator text, a key it writes is shared, so the suite's login cannot change or delete it and gets the INUSE refusal when it writes that name, and its blocking pop waits on the name as SHARED, so a push by the suite's login, which lands at suite-user's own scope, never wakes it. The tests that authenticate as such a login differ; when one of them stops while its connection is still authenticated as that login, the later tests of the unit run there too, and the acl unit's 'blocked command gets rejected when reprocessed after permission change' waits for that wake until the unit times out, so its remaining tests do not run.

categories.reason: During CLIENT PAUSE WRITE a server with labels or owners on holds every EVALSHA until the pause ends, because whether a cached script is read-only would have to be looked up before the command's scope is known, and that lookup would tell one scope about another's cache (decision R11); owner mode turns that machinery on even without a label scheme. The pause unit's test of a read-only EVALSHA under a write pause therefore waits for its reply until the suite reports no progress, which ends the unit, so the tests after it do not run.
